system.name: Rigel
system.description: The brightest star in Orion and seventh brightest in the night sky. Rigel is a blue supergiant approximately 860 light-years away, burning 120,000 times more brightly than the Sun and well on its way to becoming a supernova.

rigela.name: Rigel A
rigela.description: A B8 Ia blue supergiant roughly 79 times the Sun's diameter and one of the most intrinsically luminous stars visible to the naked eye, with a luminosity approximately 120,000 times that of the Sun. It pulsates slightly and is expected to eventually collapse into a neutron star or black hole.
rigela.funFact: Rigel is so luminous that if it were as close as Sirius, it would cast shadows on Earth at night and appear as bright as a crescent Moon.

rigelb.name: Rigel B
rigelb.description: A distant B-type companion to Rigel A, itself a close binary (Rigel Ba and Bb) separated by only a fraction of an arcsecond. The combined Rigel B system orbits Rigel A at approximately 2,200 AU — a separation so vast that their mutual orbit takes an estimated 25,000 years.
rigelb.funFact: The Rigel system is actually a triple star: Rigel A is one component, while 'Rigel B' is itself two stars (Ba and Bb) so close together they can only be separated with interferometry.
